source.note: Glucose to ethanol, draft v0: A glucose solution into a batch fermenter, then the ethanol purification train of the BioSTEAM reference designs (beer column, rectifier, molecular sieves), giving fuel-grade ethanol. The fermenter turns glucose into ethanol at the bound yield as a share of the theoretical yield, for a batch time of titre over productivity. Chemicals and finance are the dry-grind corn ethanol plant's; equipment and thermodynamics are BioSTEAM's own; no number is the flowsheet's.
the scenario this run belongs to
the dry-grind corn ethanol plant's create_chemicals, and its create_tea: ConventionalEthanolTEA with the package's default_tea_parameters
create_ethanol_purification_system as the package builds it: beer column with its heat integration, rectifier, superheater, molecular sieves, product tanks
BioSTEAM's batch bioreactor, sized and costed by BioSTEAM; its working volume fraction, cleaning time and temperature are its own, its vessel limit BioSTEAM's anaerobic bioreactor's, all read back
the fermenter's conversion is the bound yield over this reaction's yield at thermosteam's molecular weights; the run reads the theoretical yield back
the ethanol the package's molecular sieves give, with no denaturant blended; the run reads the purity back
